text:
matt.secops: heads-up — SIEM spiking with KMS decrypt failures across prod regions, started ~1930502400. lots of AccessDenied on same principal. posting sample log below

siem-bot: alert: HIGH_RATE - kms.decrypt.failures (count=1423 in 60s) ruleset=kms_ops_detector severity=high :rotating_light:

matt.secops: sample event:
```json
{
  "ts": "2026-03-03T14:01:11Z",
  "event": "KMSDecrypt",
  "status": "AccessDenied",
  "key": "projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/kr/main/cryptoKeys/kv-01",
  "principal": "serviceAccount:ephemeral-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
}
```

rory.oncall: i'm on it. paging infra and platform. are these coming from a single IP range or many? :eyes:

leah.sre: looks multi-region. grouping by principal shows same SA id repeated, but different source ips. bursty pattern every 30-60s. not a scan, more like a job retry loop.

carla.platform: we rotated ephemeral service account yesterday as part of a creds-hardening job. pipeline created new SA and we removed old key. intended to grant roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter, but i need to verify binding applied to the new SA for that specific key.

matt.secops: that matches hypothesis — if SA lost decrypt permission, apps will retry and SIEM will flood. can we confirm IAM binding and that the pipeline applied the role to the SA resource (not the project)?

carla.platform: running quick check now:
```bash
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy kv-01 --keyring=kr --location=global --project=prod | grep ephemeral-sa || true
```

carla.platform: result: no binding for ephemeral-sa on kv-01. Oops — pipeline used project-level role but key is restricted. creating binding now.

rory.oncall: while you fix, can we quiet the SIEM noise? This is drowning other alerts. proposing temporary suppression: group by principal+key and suppress if rate > 100/min for 10m with manual override. Thoughts?

emma.secmanager: temporary suppression fine but need comms. open an incident ticket, tag customers as internal-only, and annotate duration and reason. also ensure we don't mask a real attack. require correlator to check geo and source diversity before auto-suppressing.

matt.secops: agree. set suppression with these checks: requires same principal, identical key id, and no new principals over window. also add a failsafe: if any anomalous privilege escalation or unexpected envelope unwrap events appear, stop suppression.

leah.sre: i'll apply a rule tweak in SIEM: change threshold to require sustained 5-minute elevated rate and add dimension grouping (principal,key,region). will also create dashboard panel to show before/after.

siem-bot: runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/secops/siem/runbooks#kms-decrypt-flood (added incident stub)

carla.platform: binding applied to kv-01. rolling creds to affected services now. ETA ~5m.

rory.oncall: monitoring — error count dropping in region us-east1. good sign.

matt.secops: update: errors down 90% in 6m. will keep suppression active for 15m total, then let rules revert and monitor. please add postmortem action items: pipeline change to ensure per-key bindings, test harness for service account rotations, and add a CI gate verifying key-level permissions.

emma.secmanager: agreed. assign action items: carla platform - fix pipeline (owner), leah sre - SIEM rule refinement and dashboard (owner), matt secops - postmortem doc + comms (owner). deadline: EOD tomorrow.

carla.platform: filing PR for pipeline fix now, will link to incident.

leah.sre: SIEM rule updated and suppression set. will revert automatically after 15m and keep alerting on sustained anomalies. dashboard panel added: /dashboards/kms-decrypt-rate

matt.secops: closing loop: we should also ingest KMS audit log fields to make future detection richer (principal_email, iam_grant_event). adding that to the telemetry backlog. thanks all :thumbsup:

rory.oncall: :ok_hand: closing thread after postmortem created.
